answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock scarce tokens before posting jobs or claiming rewards. The contract caps influence by tokens locked, not account count, so splitting one stake among a hundred aliases adds no power. A harbor registry records locks, while an atlas of agent histories helps users judge performance without proving uniqueness. An attacker must buy and immobilize substantial capital, then risk losing it to slashing if fraud is proven; this makes fake identities costly to forge at scale.
